gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i3: Negated range formats as "^<start>-<end>"; calling toString() twice verifies caching.
ADDED i4: primes the internal iToString cache
ADDED i5: second call returns the cached string
ADDED i6: A single-char non-negated range formats as just that character (no caret, no dash).
ADDED i8: Two independently created ranges for the same single character are equal.
ADDED i9: A negated single-char range is NOT equal to a non-negated range for the same character.
ADDED i10: Negated range and non-negated range with different normalised bounds are not equal. Both factory calls receive out-of-order (high, low) arguments; the construct
ADDED i11: A negated single-char range is NOT equal to a non-negated multi-char range, even when start chars match.
ADDED i12: A range is always equal to itself (reflexive equality).
ADDED i13: A CharRange is NOT equal to an arbitrary non-CharRange object.
ADDED i15: A non-negated range does not contain a single char that lies beyond its upper bound.
ADDED i17: A single-char range does not contain a single char below its lower bound.
ADDED i19: A non-negated range cannot contain a negated range (a negated range describes a complement set).
ADDED i20: A non-negated single-char range for '�' cannot contain the negated range isNotIn('�','�'), because that negated range covers every character except '�'.
ADDED i21: A negated single-char range for space does not contain the non-negated single-char range for space.
ADDED i22: The negated range isNotIn('T','￿') excludes [T..'￿']; 'J' (74) < 'T' (84) is therefore outside the excluded interval and the range contains 'J'.
ADDED i23: A narrow negated range does not contain a wider negated range that excludes more characters.
ADDED i24: isNotIn('i', '"') — constructor swaps to start='"', end='i'
ADDED i25: A negated single-char range does not contain a negated range with completely different bounds.
ADDED i26: isNotIn('T', 'J') — constructor swaps to start='J', end='T'
ADDED i27: A negated single-char range ('1' excluded) contains a non-negated range for a different char ('J').
ADDED i28: 'J' != '1', so 'J' lies within the negated set
ADDED i29: A negated range contains itself (reflexive containment).
ADDED i30: A non-negated range contains itself (reflexive containment).
ADDED i32: A negated single-char range contains any character other than the excluded one.
ADDED i34: A single-char range contains exactly its own character.
ADDED i35: A single-char range does not contain any other character.
ADDED i38: forEach on isIn('Z','W'): the constructor swaps to start='W', end='Z'; the mock consumer absorbs each yielded character without throwing.
ADDED i39: forEach on the negated range isNotIn('T','￿') iterates without throwing.
ADDED i40: forEach on isNotIn('￸','T'): constructor swaps to start='T', end='￸'; iterates without throwing.
ADDED i41: spliterator() returns normally on the negated range isNotIn('�','ß').
ADDED i43: getEnd() returns the character used to construct a negated single-char range.
ADDED i44: getStart() returns the lower bound of a non-negated range.
ADDED i45: hashCode() completes without throwing and is consistent with equals().
